edges.label: wrong: Calls StdIn.readInt() again after the input has run out. | right: Reading after standard input is exhausted is a run-time error; test StdIn.isEmpty() before each read.

[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday 'empty' and 'done' suggest that a blank line, or pressing Enter, ends the input. For StdIn, a blank line is only whitespace: input ends only when the end-of-file signal arrives.
[1] misconception (M) -> IsEmptyMeansBlankLine: wrong rule: StdIn.isEmpty() becomes true when the user presses Enter on an empty line. Right rule: isEmpty() is true only when no tokens remain: at the end of a redirected file, or after the end-of-file sequence (<ctrl-d>, or <ctrl-z> on some systems, on a line by itself). An empty line is just whitespace.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> IsEmptyMeansBlankLine: Points to LT (isEmpty() waits until it can decide; it returns true only after end-of-file). An uneven trace ends the loop at a blank line on some passes, or counts the end-of-file keystroke as a value. (here mixing in: "StdIn.isEmpty() becomes true when the user presses Enter on an empty line")

[0] names_the_element (N): End of input is the end-of-file condition of the input stream. Typing the end-of-file sequence or reaching the end of a redirected file signals it, and StdIn.isEmpty() tests it.
[1] states_the_rule (S): isEmpty() returns true if standard input has no more values (only whitespace may be left). At a terminal the book signals the end with <ctrl-d>; the other widely used convention is <ctrl-z>.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): When isEmpty() is called at a terminal, it blocks until a token arrives (it returns false) or the end-of-file sequence is typed (it returns true). With a redirected file, it returns true right after the last token.
[1] output_prediction (OP): isEmpty() returns a boolean: true if there are no more values, false otherwise.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): isEmpty() consumes no value (at most it skips whitespace) and returns a boolean. Only the read that follows advances past a token.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): isEmpty() is the condition of the read loop, so the loop ends exactly when end-of-file is reached (<ctrl-d> at the keyboard, end of file with <).
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Role: the termination signal of a process-until-done loop, used when the amount of data is unknown.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> IsEmptyMeansBlankLine: Adding blank lines or trailing spaces at the end of the input keeps isEmpty()'s answer (still true at the end). Adding any token changes it.
[1] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Reading after the stream is exhausted is an error. Test isEmpty() first. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: Any read after the end-of-file signal or after the last token of the file.
[2] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Ending on end-of-file is right when data come from a file or a pipe, or the count is unknown. For human typists a count or a sentinel can be clearer, because the end-of-file key differs between systems.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The end must be signalled with the system's end-of-file key. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: At a terminal the user presses Enter, or uses the other system's key, so isEmpty() keeps waiting and the program seems to hang.

wrong: StdIn.isEmpty() becomes true when the user presses Enter on an empty line. | right: isEmpty() is true only when no more values remain: at the end of a redirected file, or after the end-of-file sequence (<ctrl-d>, or <ctrl-z> on some systems, on a line by itself) is typed; an empty line is just whitespace.
The read loop runs until StdIn.isEmpty() returns true, which happens when the user types the end-of-file sequence (<ctrl-d>).
